claims.text: HIS CO-AUTHOR OF TWENTY-NINE YEARS REPUDIATED THE BOOK. Peter Robbins published a statement on 13 June 2017, updated 20 June 2017. His specific allegations: a fabricated photograph purporting to show Warren with John Lennon; an altered USAF Form 490 medical appointment card on which the notation 'OPTI/RET BURN/EXP' is attributed to a 'Dr. Echols' whom Robbins says was an orthopaedic surgeon and not an ophthalmologist; signature inconsistencies on an in-processing sheet where 'Lea' is signed twice in different pens against a typed 'Lee'; and testimonial letters attributed to fellow airmen Steve LaPlume and Steve Longero that Robbins says were never sent.

claims.source: Kevin D. Randle, 'Peter Robbins Explains His Take on Left at East Gate (Part One)', A Different Perspective, http://kevinrandle.blogspot.com/2017/08/peter-robbins-explains-his-take-on-left_10.html , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: WHAT THE REPUDIATION CONCEDES, AND IT MUST BE CARRIED. Robbins accepts as authentic the handwritten letter Warren wrote to his mother in January 1981 and states that its authenticity 'does not mean that everything else Warren has said or written follows in kind'. Robbins also records that the military paperwork he examined was supplied by Warren and was 'mostly Xerox copies with some originals'. So the honest position is not that Warren was never at Bentwaters; it is that his presence at the events, and the documents he produced for it, are what is disputed.

label: Larry Warren
narrative: Larry Warren is carried here for the dispute rather than for the claim, because the dispute is documented and the claim is not. What is not in dispute is his assignment: his own co-author, after repudiating almost everything else, still accepts as authentic the handwritten letter Warren sent his mother in January 1981 and says explicitly that its authenticity does not carry the rest. What is in dispute is his presence at the events and the documentary evidence he produced for it. The case against him was not assembled by sceptics. Peter Robbins wrote Left at East Gate with him and defended it for twenty-nine years before publishing a statement on 13 June 2017 alleging, among other things, that a USAF Form 490 in the book's evidence carries an ophthalmic notation attributed to a physician Robbins found to be an orthopaedic surgeon, that a photograph purporting to show Warren with John Lennon is fabricated, that signatures on an in-processing sheet do not match, and that testimonial letters attributed to two named fellow airmen were never sent. Four months later the publisher, Cosimo, Inc., announced it was suspending distribution of the book because some of the experiences described in it 'may be inaccurate or embellished'. The senior officer on the record, Col. Charles Halt, is reported as saying Warren was not there; that strand reaches this board only through summaries and is graded Tier 3 until something Halt wrote is opened. The Briefing Document's own editorial header asserts that Warren is corroborated by Nick Pope, Lord Hill-Norton and Clifford Stone, but two of those three are witnesses inside the same document and one of them is Stone, whose service record is on this board.
